annotations.title: Hauing diligently atteined.
annotations.text: [1] Hereby vve ſee that, though the Holy Ghoſt ruled the penne of holy vvriters that they might not erre, yet did they vſe humane meanes to ſearch out and find the truth of the things they wrote of. Euen ſo doe Councels, and the Preſident of them, Gods vicar, diſcuſſe and examine al cauſes by humane meanes, the aſſiſtance of the Holy Ghoſt concurring and directing them into al truth, according to Chriſtes promiſe Io. 16, 13: as in the very firſt Councel of the Apoſtles them ſelues at Hieruſalem is manifeſt Act. 15, 7 and 28. Againe here we haue a familiar preface of the Author as to his frende, or to euery godly Reader (ſignified by Theophilus) concerning the cauſe and purpoſe and maner of his writing, and yet the very ſame is confeſſed Scripture, vvith the whole booke folowing. Maruel not then if the Author of [2] the ſecond booke of the Machabees [3] vſe the like humane ſpeaches both at the beginning and in the later end, neither do thou therfore reiect the booke for no Scripture, as our Heretikes doe: or not thinke him a ſacred writer.

notes.text: The second booke of the Machabees.

annotations.title: Iuſt before God.
annotations.text: Againſt the Heretikes of this time, here is it euident that holy men be iuſt, not only by the eſtimation of men, but in deede and before God.

annotations.title: In al the commaundements.
annotations.text: Three things to be noted directly againſt the Heretikes of our time. firſt, that good men doe keepe al Gods commaundements: which (they ſay) are impoſſible to be kept. <mn>◦</mn> Againe, that men be iuſtified not by only imputation of Chriſtes iuſtice, nor by faith alone, but by walking in the commaundements. Againe, that the keeping and doing of the commaundements is properly our iuſtification.

notes.text: True justification by observing the commandments.

annotations.title: Iuſtifications.
annotations.text: This word is ſo vſual in the Scriptures (namely in the Pſal. 118) to ſignifie the commaundements of God, becauſe the keeping of them is iuſtificatió, and the Greeke is alwaies ſo fully correſpondent to the ſame, [1] that the Heretikes in this place (other-wiſe pretending to eſteeme much of the Greeke) [2] bluſh not to ſay, that they auoid this word of purpoſe againſt the iuſtification of the Papiſts. And therfore one vſeth Tullies word forſooth, in Latin conſtituta: and his ſcholers in their Engliſh Bibles [3] ſay, Ordinances.

annotations.title: Ioy and exultation.
annotations.text: This was fulfilled, not only when he was borne, but now alſo through the whole Church for euer, in ioyful celebrating of his Natiuitie.

annotations.title: He departed.
annotations.text: In the old Law (ſaith S. Hierom) they that offered hoſtes for the people, were not only not in their houſes, but were purified for the time, being ſeparated from their wiues, and they dranke neither wine nor any ſtrong drinke, which are wont to prouoke concupiſcence. [1] Much more the Prieſts of the new Law that muſt alwaies offer ſacrifices, muſt alwaies be free from matrimonie. Li. 1 c. 19. adu. Iouin. and ep. 50 c. 3. See S. Ambroſe in 1 Tim. 3. And therfore if there were any religion in [2] Caluins Communion, they would at the leaſt giue as much reuerence in this point, as they in the old Law did to their ſacrifices, and to the loaues of propoſition. 1 Reg. 21.

notes.text: Ministers not so perfect as the Priests of the old law.

annotations.title: Haile ful of grace.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> Holy Church and al true Chriſtian men doe much and often vſe theſe wordes brought from heauen by the Archangel, as wel to the honour of Chriſt and our B. Ladie, as alſo for that they were the wordes of the firſt glad tidings of Chriſts Incarnation and our Saluation by the ſame, and be the very abridgement and ſumme of the whole Goſpel. In ſo much that the Greeke Church vſed it daily in the Maſſe. <mn>[2]</mn>

annotations.title: Ful of grace.
annotations.text: [1] Note the excellent prerogatiues of our B. Lady, and abhorre thoſe Heretikes which make her no better then other vulgar women, and therfore to take from her fulnes of grace, they ſay here, Haile freely beloued, contrarie to al ſignifications of the Greeke word, which is at the leſt, endued with grace, as S. Paul vſeth it Epheſ. 1. by S. Chryſoſtoms interpretation: or rather, ful of grace, as both [2] [3] Greeke and Latin fathers haue alwaies here vnderſtood it, and the Latines alſo read it, namely S. Ambroſe thus, Wel is ſhe only called ful of grace, who only obteined the grace, which no other woman deſerued, to be repleniſhed with the author of grace. And if they did as wel know the nature of theſe kind of Greeke wordes, as they would ſeeme very ſkilful, they might eaſily obſerue that they ſignifie fulnes, [4]as when them ſelues tranſlate the like word (Luc. 16, 20) ful of ſores. Beza, vlceroſus.

notes.text: S. Athan. de S. Deip. S. Ephrem in orat. de laud. B. virg. Ambro. in 1 Luc. li. 2. Hier, ep. 140 in exp. Ps. 44.

annotations.title: I know not man.
annotations.text: ◦ Theſe wordes declare (ſaith S. Auguſtine) that ſhe had now vowed virginitie to God. For otherwiſe neither would ſhe ſay, How ſhal this be done? nor haue added, becauſe I know not man. Yea if ſhe had ſaid only the firſt wordes, How ſhal this be done? it is euident that ſhe would not haue aſked ſuch a queſtion, how a vvoman ſhould beare a ſonne promiſed her, if ſhe had married meaning to haue carnal copulation. c. 4 de virgin. As if he ſhould ſay, If ſhe might haue knowen a man and ſo haue had a childe, ſhe vvould neuer haue aſked, How ſhal this be done? but becauſe that ordinarie way vvas excluded by her vow of virginitie, therfore ſhe aſketh, How? And in aſking, How? ſhe plainly declareth that ſhe might not haue a childe by knowing man, becauſe of her vow. See S. Grego. Nyſſene de ſancta Chriſti Natiuitate.

annotations.title: Eliſabeth thy Coſin.
annotations.text: ◦ By this that Eliſabeth and our Lady were coſins, the one of the tribe of Leui, the other of Iuda, is gathered that Chriſt came of both tribes, Iuda and Leui, of the kings and the prieſts: him ſelf both a king and a prieſt, and the Anointed (to wit) by grace ſpiritually, as they were with oile materially and corporally. Auguſt. 2 de Conſens. Euang. c. 1.

notes.text: Christ came of both tribes, Iuda and Leui.

annotations.title: Bleſſed art thou.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> At the very hearing of our Ladies voice, the infant and ſhe were repleniſhed with the Holy Ghoſt, and ſhe ſang praiſes not only to Chriſt, but for his ſake to our B. Lady, calling her bleſſed and her fruite bleſſed, as the Church doeth alſo by her wordes and example in the <sc>AVE MARIE</sc>.

annotations.title: Mother of my Lord.
annotations.text: ◦ Elizabeth being an exceding iuſt and bleſſed woman, yet the worthines of Gods mother doth ſo far excel her and al other women, as the great light the litle ſtarres. Hiero. Præf. in Sophon.

annotations.title: Shal call me bleſſed.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> This Prophecie is fulfilled, when the Church keepeth her Feſtiual daies, and when the faithful in al generations ſay the <sc>AVE MARIE</sc>, and other holy Antems of our Lady. And therfore the Caluiniſtes are not among thoſe generations which call our Lady bleſſed.

notes.text: Her honour in al the world.

annotations.title: Iohn is his name.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> Wee ſee that names are of ſignification and importance, God him ſelf changing or giuing names in both Teſtaments: as, Abraham, Iſrael, Peter, and the principal of al others, <sc>IESVS</sc>: and here <sc>IOHN</sc>, which ſignifieth, Gods grace or mercie, or, God wil haue mercie. For he was the Precurſor and Prophet of the mercie and grace that enſued by <sc>CHRIST IESVS</sc>. Note alſo that as then in Circunciſion, ſo now in Baptiſme (which anſwereth therevnto) names are giuen. <mn>[2]</mn> And as we ſee here and in al the old Teſtament, great reſpect was had of names: ſo we muſt beware of ſtrange, profane, and ſecular names (now a daies to common) and rather according to the <mn>[3]</mn> Catechiſme of the holy Councel of Trent, take names of Saincts and holy men, that may put vs in minde of their vertues.

notes.text: What names to be giuen in Baptisme.

annotations.title: Iuſtice before him.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> Here alſo we ſee that we may haue true iuſtice, not only in the ſight of men, or by the imputation of God, but in deede before him and in his ſight: and that the comming of Chriſt was to giue men ſuch iuſtice.

annotations.title: The orient.
annotations.text: <mn>[1]</mn> Maruel not if Heretikes controule the old authentical tranſlation, as though it differed from the greeke: whereas here they make much a doe to controule not only al the greeke interpreters of the old teſtament, but alſo S. Luke him ſelf, for the word ἀνατολὴ, as differing from the Hebrew. <mn>[2]</mn>

notes.text: The Heretikes controule both Greeke and Latin text.
